steps.content: On the outskirts of Eastside, wild grass runs rampant. A few drab, weathered buildings hunch silently under the midday glare.
Quick, measured footsteps approach and then stop dead outside an abandoned factory. Without a word, the pursuit team leader signals, and the squad dissolves along the wall, melting into position.

You press against a pillar by the door. In your earpiece, nothing but a thin static hiss. From an old residential block nearby, a TV news report leaks through the silence, its voice fraying in and out.

steps.speaker: News
steps.content: ...Eastside's academic community has been rocked by yet another scandal. Renowned scholar Professor Morris has been taken into custody by the Public Security Bureau, formally charged with years of academic fraud. According to sources, a whistleblower has provided multiple news outlets with a complete body of evidence, including photographs, audio recordings, and comparative data analysis...
Behind you, the squad holds its breath, dark muzzles trained on the rusty iron door. Even through its thick bulk, you can feel clearly the restless Mania energy churning on the other side.
The team captain flashes you a signal, fingers curling into a fist. All exits sealed.
You answer with a flat palm held low, then slice it quietly forward.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Copy. On my signal.

steps.speaker: News
steps.content: ...Morris has since provided authorities with the names of multiple individuals involved in the case. Among those mentioned repeatedly is a mysterious supplier operating under the alias "Pixel." Sources familiar with the matter indicate that this individual has long been active on the dark web, with an extensive range of services...
You raise your hand.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Three, two...

steps.speaker: News
steps.content: ...The true identity of "Pixel," however, remains a mystery. Some believe the suspect is an individual deeply familiar with Eastside's academic community and highly skilled with the internet. Others suggest the alias may not belong to a single person, but could instead be an outsourcing front for an entire organization...

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: One! Breach!
Bam!
The iron door crashes down. In the same instant, the squad pours into the factory under the cover of smoke, weapons raised, all trained on the figure at the center of the room.

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Freeze! Drop everything. Hands where I can see...

steps.speaker: Eugene
steps.content: Wha—?!
The acrid smoke thins and the room sharpens. And the captain's warning dies mid-sentence, like a duck strangled silent.

At the center of the room, hunched over a battered computer, is someone who looks exactly like Pixel's online avatar from the case file. She hears the commotion and, after a stiff delay, creaks her head around.
A girl's body, topped with a computer head. Unsettling doesn't quite cover it. Where a face should be, a screen glows and stutters, endlessly flickering.

She spots the squad, and her pixel features cycle through expressions in quick succession: [startled], [confused], then [shocked]. You stare at her, and she... and the pixel dots on the screen stare back.
No time to process. You unleash the shackles on this high M-Value threat without hesitation. Just as relief begins to settle in your chest at the clean capture, she moves.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Don't kill me! Don't kill me!

The computer head girl hits the floor with a thud, then scrambles over on all fours and latches onto your leg. Her screen strobes through a frantic carousel of weeping pixel faces, while her very human body writhes and clings. The whole scene feels less like an arrest and more like stumbling onto the set of a horror film.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: I'll talk! I'll tell you everything! Three deposits this afternoon, that's all I took! I told those fossils I was totally trustworthy, but the whole time I was recording every single word!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: The files are all on this computer. Except it's dead, because I dropped potato chip crumbs in the fan and the whole thing, hard drive included, just decided to explode! But my backup folder! My backup folder is called "Little Girl and the Digital Werewolf." Romantic, right? A little sci-fi, a little tragic? You have to admit it's got flair.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: I've read manga with this exact plot... Ah! I am cooperating! I'm the most cooperative! Please don't kill me, I'm begging you. When you really think about it, I'm just a monitor. A screen with legs!
The nonsense keeps spilling out. Incoherent, erratic, scared witless and utterly unhinged... Is she really a high M-Value Sinner?
You watch the so-called mysterious broker thrash across the floor, wailing from her throat and her screen in stereo. Words fail you. Only one thought remains:
...No way this lunatic is Pixel. The Pixel who could upend everything in Eastside academia... You've got to be kidding me...
The guards march Pixel to the interrogation room and shove her into the chair. Her mouth hasn't stopped running the entire way.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: So your elevator, is it encrypted? Because I tried to ping a signal when the doors opened, and it didn't just block me. It bounced me right back! Internal comms, right? What happens during a blackout? Do you get a private elevator, Chief? A sea-view suite up on the twenty-eighth floor, very corporate president chic?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: What's the official policy on housing Sinners? Am I staying long? Asking for my screen, mostly. The lighting in here is very hostile to my color calibration. I'm a warm-tone girl, honestly, and this place is all cold fluorescents. If I start flickering or getting dead pixels, does the Bureau cover repairs?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh! And this chair! The texture is amazing. Seriously, my studio is desperate for a chair like this. My last one had a screw that just quietly gave up on life, and one day I went for a dramatic roll backward and, bam, total wipeout!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: See this? This dent right here on my head? That was the floor's fault... Took me forever to find a matching paint!
You sit across the table and watch her performance in silence. The case file from the Public Security Bureau lies open before you.

Professor Morris's scandal didn't unravel from within. Someone leaked it straight to the press. Once the public firestorm hit, all the usual academic damage control became impossible. The Public Security Bureau had to step in under full public glare and make the arrest fast.

During interrogation, Morris flipped. Hoping to reduce his sentence, he coughed up a long list of names. Pixel's was on it. A preliminary check flagged her as a suspected Sinner, so the case was transferred to you.

Tucked inside the case file is a photo, a screenshot from the dark web chat interface. The account's avatar is a glitching monitor with a cheeky pixel art tongue-out emoji. The person wearing the monitor for a head throws a peace sign with one hand and flips the bird with the other.
Miss Pixel, please mind yourself. I'm the one asking questions here. You're not running a Q&A about MBCC.
You slap the file down on the table and cut through her rambling with a cold, level voice.
Only then does she seem to remember where she is. The pixel expression on her screen stutters once and flips to an innocent smile.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh, don't be so grumpy. I'm being super cooperative right now.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Pixel! That's the full thing, no surname. But you can mix it up if you want. Pix-el. Pi-xel. Pixe-l. They all work. Each one's got a different vibe, right? All easy to remember.
Stay on topic. What are you wearing on your head?
Her screen responds instantly. The pixel expression flips to a heart, with pink bubbles floating up in a steady stream.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: It's a statement piece. Modern art. It's called symbolism, maybe you've heard of it? This is my tribute to the father of the Internet. Bless that man. Without him, how would I ever express the full spectrum of my dazzling personality with such precision?
...Tell me about your ability.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Does it have to be about my ability? Because if I had to pick a position here at the Bureau, I'd want admin. Totally serious. Admin staff hear everything. They know all the secrets. Like, for example, do you ever dance in your office when your favorite team wins?

Pixel does not acknowledge that this is an interrogation. Her answers veer between irrelevant and inventively insane, delivered with total conviction. Every threat, every lure, every pressure point you push lands soft, swallowed whole like a fist into cotton. Each time you think you have her pinned, she squirms away in some new direction.
You take a breath, steady yourself, and switch tactics.
Alright. Let's talk about something else, then. Your name came up a lot in the files the Public Security Bureau sent over.
You leaf through the documents in your hand. The inventory is meticulous.

...Ghostwriting papers. Fabricating experimental data. Getting prohibited materials into university labs. Student essays, tenure reviews, quick graduation projects, long-term contraband supply... You've got your hands in everything, don't you?
That's quite the business you're running, Miss Pixel. Very full-service.
Pixel responds with a bashful little wave of her hand.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Full-service? Well... I wouldn't say I do everything. But honestly? I do most things.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Ghostwriting, data fabrication, sneaking restricted materials into university labs right under their noses... That's not even my core business anymore.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Anybody can train a monkey to type. Two hands, a keyboard, and zero morals? Dime a dozen. The real money is in being the one who knows things and connects people.
That's why you chose to do everything online?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Obviously! I mean, I did think about going offline at first. House calls, face-to-face, very boutique. But thank the father of the Internet, I went digital instead. That's where I built my modest but extremely profitable little domain!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Offline is so dangerous anyway. One wrong turn and someone corners you in an alley, and then what? But behind a screen? Behind a screen I'm untouchable. Total control!
Her voice suddenly drops. The pixelated face on her screen tilts to a new angle, with light and shadow splitting across the display.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: No one finds me. No one catches me. That's the whole point.

You remember the file. The Public Security Bureau's preliminary investigation had already linked the name Pixel to a trail of academic cases, big and small. The client list she had cultivated over the years carried enough weight to crack the entire power structure of academia wide open.
A loose cannon like that, volatile and unpredictable. There must have been no shortage of people who wanted her gone.
I see. So you somehow stuck a computer on your head as a disguise to keep anyone from figuring out who you really are?
Pixel smacks the side of her head with a loud pop. The screen snaps back to that carefree grin.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Wrong! One hundred percent wrong! It's not a disguise, it's a brand! Instantly recognizable, completely iconic! And for the last time, I. Was. Born. With. This. Computer. Head.
...You can't seriously expect me to believe that.
Pixel ignores your remark entirely. She reaches up and taps a finger playfully against the monitor at her neck. A rose colored pixel bird appears on the screen and immediately breaks into song.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: ♪ I'm a little bird, flying free, a soul that no one'll ever find... My virtual face became my real one, and now I float along, among the streams of data... ♪ Haha! That's a good one! A Pixel like this does whatever she wants, and no one gets to say otherwise!
Her bright voice crackles with a grainy, electronic edge. Right now, she has decided she is a machine, and the interrogation room is her stage.

You watch this strange, erratic creature drift in and out of her own world and still cannot square her with the underground legend who allegedly holds half of Eastside's academia in her palm. The file in your hands begins to feel less like fact and more like a bet someone else made.
The things Professor Morris accused you of. Did you actually do all of that?

You push the confession toward her. Plain as day, right there in ink. Morris states that Pixel provided prohibited materials and falsified data across several experiments. A final handoff was scheduled for today—the remaining materials and one critical dataset.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh, absolutely. Every single thing you've found about me so far? All me. What he told you I did? I did it. What he didn't tell you I did? I did that too.
You narrow your eyes. A keyword in her words snags your attention.
"What he didn't tell you." What's that supposed to mean?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Ahhh, well, I mean...
She spreads her hands. The pixel mouth on her screen pops open into a perfectly innocent circle.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: See, the professor came to me the summer before last. Referral from a regular, very hush-hush. His project was something about biochemical emissions from tiny insects. He wanted to publish in the "S" academic journal. The one where landing a paper basically makes you a god of the field overnight. You've heard of it, right, Chief?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: He told me if I could get him published, he'd throw in a bonus this much on top of my regular fee! And of course I said yes! Who says no to money? I'm not an idiot. But here's the thing that's been tickling my circuits ever since... Where does a university professor get that kind of funding?

Pixel mumbles to herself, ticking numbers off on her fingers, then suddenly looks up. Her monitor suddenly floods with transaction logs, billing statements, and chat records, scrolling past in an eager, relentless parade.
Miss Pixel, forgive me for cutting in. But you do realize all this evidence you're so proudly showing off works just as well to prove your own guilt, right?
Every time the gods close all the doors on me, I always find a tiny crack. You made this possible for me.
You're laying all this out for me. You want to spend the rest of your life in a cell?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: ...Huh?
She freezes. The pixel face on her screen lags like a bad signal, mouth hanging half open, staring at you as if her brain is still loading.
Satisfied, you ease back into your chair and change tack.

Here's the thing, though. You hand over your full client list and cooperate with the investigation, and I can put in a word for you. MBCC has always been willing to go easy on Sinners who've lost their way.

The girl's digital expression lurches from stunned to panicked, then from panicked to eager. But caught between those two frames, something else flashes, a look that is gone so fast you almost doubt you saw it at all.

The next second, she scrambles to pull up every file she has, thrusting both hands forward in offering, while her pixel face squeezes out a fawning grin so theatrical it practically dares you to believe it.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Take it, take it, take it! It's all yours! Please, please, Chief, don't throw me in prison! I'm way too young for prison! I haven't even saved up enough to buy out every potato chip company in Eastside yet!

Yet something about her breathless tone and the pink bubbles swarming her screen feels off. It's too eager. Not the eagerness of fear, but of someone who has been waiting for you to say those exact words.
But you don't have time to linger on it. The name list is already on your terminal, each entry tagged with a neat service note.

Harold, Dean of Life Sciences: tenure paper ghostwriting, publication report fabrication. Lennard, Senior Professor of Theoretical Biology: prohibited lab equipment purchase, experimental data falsification. Philip, Associate Dean of the Institute of Advanced Life Studies: paper authorship for sale, student appeal management ...
It reads like a roll call of every notable name in Eastside academia, all gathered in one place.
You read on, torn between disgust and astonishment at the grime beneath those polished titles, until a single line of notes pins your gaze in place.
Your head snaps up.

options: This record right here. Is it accurate?

choices.text: This record right here. Is it accurate?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Wittmann. The big, big name in biochemistry. Mania-contaminated biological material purchase... Ohhh, that's what grabbed you, huh?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: It was fairly recent, actually. He placed the order with me, but the supplier was someone else, though. I'm just the friendly neighborhood middleman.
A cold weight settles in you. This is no longer about falsified data or bought authorships. Mania-contaminated materials mean the red line has been crossed. A bomb with a lit fuse.
Do you know what he was experimenting on?
You frown, the weight of it pressing into your voice. Pixel answers with the same airy lilt she might use to comment on a sunny afternoon.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: How should I know? It's Mania, sweetheart, the clue's in the name!

Every alarm in your head blares at once. If Pixel is telling the truth, this man is not falsifying research anymore. He is engineering a disaster. An academic giant with access to Mania-contaminated materials, working out of an unsecured university lab. Every second that passes is a countdown.
He needs to be arrested. Now.
There is no time to waste. You file for an emergency deployment order and head to Eastside University, Pixel in tow.

For most students, this is just another ordinary day. The sun is warm, the tree-lined paths dappled with light and shadow. They cross the campus with books and laptops cradled in their arms, their faces full of the bright, untroubled future they still believe in.
Just before the lab door, Pixel stops and turns. The pixel face on her screen resolves into a knowing smile.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: You know what, Chief? In a place like this, you open a door thinking you're walking toward knowledge. Truth is, more often than not, you're walking straight into hell.
The unspoken thing in her words hangs in your mind, but before you can voice it, Pixel shoves the door open and steps inside.

Professor Wittmann stands at the lab bench, a titan of biochemistry known across academia, calmly organizing documents. He looks up at the intrusion. His eyes pass over you and pause on Pixel. For the briefest moment, something breaks through his composure. Then it seals over, and he is unreadable again.
You hold up your badge and identify yourself.

MBCC has received evidence of your purchase of Mania-contaminated materials. We have reason to believe you are conducting unauthorized Mania experiments. We ask that you cooperate fully with our investigation.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: There must be some misunderstanding. My research has nothing whatsoever to do with Mania. You're welcome to search the lab. You won't find a thing.

He adjusts his glasses, his voice perfectly level. A faint, condescending smirk tugs at the corner of his mouth, as if your words are too absurd to dignify. Then his gaze shifts back to Pixel, and he lets out a sneer.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: I know who you are. The little digital ghost. Every grubby scandal that's dragged Eastside's academic community through the mud, you've had your fingers in it somewhere. Utterly contemptible.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: And now the authorities are working hand in hand with a criminal. What an extraordinary partnership. Is this how you clear your name, then? Slap together a few false accusations and drag the entire academic world down with you? What exactly are you hoping to get out of this?

Whether the Mania experiments are real is something we'll determine through our investigation. But that aside, Professor Morris gave up your name when he was taken into custody. You're implicated in the academic misconduct. That much isn't in dispute. So save the righteous indignation until after you've been cleared.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: I'm aware of that. And I have already cooperated fully with the investigation. The data falsification in my research, that's something I cannot deny. But I am deeply troubled by all of this, because the matter itself...

He steps aside just enough to show what was behind him.
In the corner, a gaunt girl stands hunched in a rumpled lab coat. Her fingers knot together, knuckles blanched bone white. Her face is the color of raw plaster.
Wittmann shakes his head, his voice thickening with a show of disappointment.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: How could you... falsify the work of an entire lab, just to get the results you wanted? I've told you from day one: if you want to stand in this field, first you have to stand as a person of integrity.

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: Of all people... I never imagined it would be you. My most dutiful, well-behaved student. And to think I only learned what you'd done when the investigators came knocking and laid every last ugly mistake out in the open.
The girl trembles uncontrollably, her lip caught hard between her teeth. No words come.
There are no words that would help. The lab drops into a heavy silence, every gaze fixed on her like a stain on a coat bleached a hundred times.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Enough.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh come on, this trick again? After all these years, you still haven't gotten sick of it?
Her voice is not particularly loud, but every syllable cuts through the room, cold and sardonic. She sounds like a completely different person from the manic girl of minutes ago.
The whole lab freezes, every head swiveling toward the strange figure with the computer head.

Pixel stands in the doorway. The pixel face on her screen holds no discernible expression, yet you can read it all the same. Contempt, loathing, and underneath... a faint trace of weariness. The way one watches a spent clown who should have exited the stage long ago.
Pixel seems delighted to have the spotlight. A cheerful chime rings out as a tiny golden lightbulb pops onto her screen.

She claps her hands, strides lightly to the center of the lab, and with one swift motion sweeps every document off the table. Then she hops onto the edge and swings her legs like a child on a park bench.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Alright, everyone! You've been working so hard. How about a little break? Come play the mini-game Pixel just finished coding! No wipes, no paywalls, completely free to test. Try not to cry. It's just a developer pouring her heart and soul out for you!

A breezy, slightly off-kilter electronic jingle fills the air as Pixel extends her hands. Above her palms, white pixel cubes flicker into existence and stack themselves in neat layers, like a 3D printer weaving something out of nothing.
A vintage projector solidifies in her grip. She clicks the switch, and a curtain of light unfurls in midair.
Through the shimmering colors, crooked letters bounce into view, wobbling like pellets from a game of Snake.
Life in Academia
